source.title: The jamming transition as a paradigm to understand the loss landscape of deep neural networks
source.authors: M. Geiger; Stefano Spigler; Stéphane d'Ascoli; Levent Sagun; Marco Baity-Jesi; G. Biroli; M. Wyart

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains fully connected networks across parameter counts and measures fitting, loss, and misclassification around a jamming transition. This conceptually tests training-error and depth claims, but uses binary classification, different datasets and protocols from the claim versions' cited benchmarks.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own training and fitting results, not cited results. The reported CIFAR-10 loss comparison is an auxiliary architecture-performance result and does not measure training classification error for a claim version. Hyperparameter and initialization sensitivity statements without reported outcome rows are summarized in method_sensitivity.
record.test_reason: The study measures fitting transitions in fully connected binary classifiers. V1 specifies convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100; the other versions specify comparisons or dynamics this study does not measure. Its initialization caveats and use of batch normalization do not test initialization-dependent speed or depth, or normalization's acceleration.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors report a jamming transition separating complete fitting from positive hinge loss in fully connected networks, with fitting thresholds approximately independent of tested depth. Their explanation excluding poor minima assumes sufficiently many effective parameters and preserved signal propagation. Poor initialization is a theoretical caveat, not a reported controlled initialization experiment; positive hinge loss also need not imply misclassification.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines binary classification with fully connected networks, random data and reduced binary MNIST; it varies parameter count and measures fitting transitions, rather than reproducing CIFAR benchmark training recipes or the cited methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The transition location has mild dependence on optimizer, batch size, and learning-rate schedule. Cross-entropy uses PyTorch default initialization, SGD, batch normalization, and a specified schedule; hinge uses orthogonal initialization, ADAM, full batches, no normalization, and another schedule. At small training times, errors remain for large P. The paper warns that poor initialization that prevents signal propagation can produce finite-loss minima.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected binary classifiers fit all training examples above a parameter threshold. For random data, the threshold scales approximately linearly with sample count after sufficiently long training; short training budgets can leave errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected binary networks exhibit a training-budget-dependent transition to complete fitting as parameter count increases.

fits_no_version.finding: The number of margin violations per parameter jumps at the fitting transition, while misclassification grows smoothly with loss; margin violations need not be classification errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin satisfaction and classification accuracy have different behavior near the jamming transition in fully connected binary networks.

fits_no_version.finding: For reduced binary MNIST, the minimum parameter count allowing complete classification is approximately independent of tested depth and smaller than for random data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter budget, additional depth does not materially improve complete-fitting capacity in the tested fully connected random-data and binary MNIST settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Few small negative Hessian eigenvalues remain after prolonged tanh-network training in an underparameterized random-data setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prolonged optimization can approach nearly nonnegative Hessian curvature in underparameterized tanh networks without establishing complete fitting.

record.problems: The study tests binary fully connected setups rather than CIFAR-10/100. The principal initialization comparison is confounded by loss and training recipe. Transition locations are mostly figure-based without tabulated numerical values, and the paper notes unconverged dynamics near P/N ∈ [2.8, 2.9] and errors at small training times.
record.rows_left_out: The auxiliary Shake-Shake CIFAR-10 comparison reports test error for cross-entropy and hinge-loss runs (Section II.B), not training classification error or one of the versioned behaviors, so it was not extracted as a row.

untested.parts: Training classification error of sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and the specified smaller-model, early-stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious-local-minimum frequencies in realizable two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth, including matched orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons and very deep convolutional training.
Loss and curvature trajectories relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery, divergence and edge-of-stability behavior.
Controlled effects of batch normalization on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. Differences in architecture and dataset are outside the versions' stated scope, rather than evidence limiting that scope. Confounded initialization recipes and batch normalization's presence are untested comparisons, not limits_scope results. States marked cannot_determine concern the supplied claim versions; they do not reject the study's reported fitting transitions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fitting and misclassification with random binary labels and binary MNIST labels, but not CIFAR-10/100, random-label memorization on those benchmarks, or the cited SGD/Adam recipes as specified.

Compares default initialization for cross-entropy with orthogonal initialization for hinge loss, not matched activation-specific initializations or orthogonal versus Gaussian weights at equal variance; no 10,000-layer network result.
Batch normalization is used only for the cross-entropy random-data experiment; no controlled comparison of speed or learning-rate tolerance with and without normalization.

rows.subject: fully-connected network, random data, cross-entropy loss
rows.size_stated: varied; N* vs P, numerical sizes not stated in text
rows.operation_detail: Reduced width at fixed depth until all data could no longer be classified within the selected learning time; recorded transition N* against P.

conditions.value: random inputs on d-dimensional hyper-sphere; random labels yµ = ±1
varied; Fig. 5(b) depths and dimensions as indicated in figure

rows.measure: Transition parameter count N* at which loss approaches zero / all data fit
rows.value: N* increases approximately linearly with P at long learning times; the transition lies below the stated theoretical upper bound P/N* = 1/2 − Nc/N.
rows.note: The paper says large P at small times retains errors, and reports the transition as little dependent on depth and input dimension. Figure-specific per-setting values are not reconstructed.
rows.check: Fully connected random-data classifiers do not match V1's convolutional CIFAR setting. The transition is defined by correct classification within the training budget; cross-entropy remains positive at finite weights, so zero loss must not be equated with this transition.

rows.subject: fully-connected network, random data, hinge loss
rows.size_stated: varied; N* vs P, numerical sizes not stated in text
rows.operation_detail: Reduced width at fixed depth until the network could no longer classify all data within the selected learning time; recorded transition N* against P.

conditions.value: random inputs and random labels yµ = ±1
starting at 10−4, divided by 10 every 250k steps

rows.measure: Transition parameter count N* at which fitting changes from zero loss to nonzero loss
rows.value: Results are described as very similar to those for cross-entropy; transition shown in Fig. 5(c), with stated upper bound P/N* = 1/2 − Nc/N.
rows.note: The prose gives a qualitative comparison and bound, not individual transition values.
rows.check: The fitting transition is an empirical result, but concerns fully connected binary classifiers rather than V1's convolutional CIFAR networks.

rows.subject: fully-connected ReLU networks, random data
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of unsatisfied constraints NΔ/N as P/N and training time varied around the transition.
rows.note: The paper states the dynamics had not converged for P/N ∈ [2.8, 2.9]; this row records the reported stationary regimes.
rows.check: NΔ/N counts margin violations per parameter, not training classification error. A violated margin can still correspond to a correctly classified example. The architecture and data also fall outside V1.

rows.subject: fully-connected ReLU networks, random data
rows.operation_detail: Measured number of misclassified data against loss near the fitting transition.
rows.value: Increases monotonically and initially very slowly with loss; unsatisfied constraints do not immediately cause misclassification.
rows.note: Near the transition, positive gaps can be unsatisfied while still correctly classified; the number misclassified therefore does not itself fully track constraint satisfaction.
rows.check: The qualitative misclassification-versus-loss relationship concerns fully connected random-data classifiers, outside V1. Its smooth growth does not itself establish a partial near-zero-error effect.

rows.subject: fully-connected tanh network, random data
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 10 million and 100 million ADAM steps and counted negative Hessian eigenvalues at the end.
rows.value: After 10 million steps, 11 negative eigenvalues between −5 · 10−5 and −2 · 10−8; after 100 million, 6 between −4 · 10−6 and −2 · 10−8.
rows.note: This measures Hessian curvature, not training classification error or loss, so it cannot establish the V1 fitting outcome.
rows.check: Remaining negative Hessian eigenvalues measure curvature, not V1's training error, V2's teacher-student local-minimum frequency, or V5's learning-rate-dependent stability dynamics.

rows.subject: fully-connected network, MNIST binary classification
rows.stage_stated: trained with hinge loss; initialization not stated in this section
rows.operation_detail: Varied number of patterns P at fixed network size and measured unsatisfied constraints around the transition.

conditions.value: MNIST, first 10 PCA components; even versus odd digits
same gradient descent dynamics as described above

rows.value: Jumps discontinuously as P/N increases; transition density NΔ/N ≈ 0.5.
rows.note: Binary MNIST fitting setup, not CIFAR or multiclass classification.
rows.check: The experiment uses fully connected binary MNIST classifiers, outside V1. Its measure counts margin violations per parameter rather than misclassification.

rows.subject: fully-connected network, MNIST binary classification
rows.stage_stated: trained with hinge loss; initialization not stated in this section
rows.operation_detail: Measured number of misclassified data against loss.

conditions.value: MNIST, first 10 PCA components; even versus odd digits

rows.note: The reported metric is misclassification count across the loss sweep, not a numerical training-error value at each setting.
rows.check: The misclassification relationship is measured on reduced binary MNIST with fully connected networks, outside V1. Smooth growth with loss alone does not warrant a partial state.

rows.subject: fully-connected networks, MNIST binary classification
rows.size_stated: varied width h and parameter count N*
rows.stage_stated: trained with hinge loss; initialization not stated in this section
rows.operation_detail: Varied network size and depth to find the lowest parameter count N* at which all patterns could still be classified correctly.
rows.measure: Minimum parameter count N* to fit data
rows.value: N* is essentially independent of depth, especially at larger P; it is significantly smaller than for random data.
rows.note: The authors describe finding the lowest N* for which all patterns could still be classified correctly.
rows.check: The minimum parameter count for fitting reduced binary MNIST is outside V1. Depth independence at fixed parameter count also does not test V3's plain versus residual convolutional training comparison.

rows.subject: fully-connected network, random data, cross-entropy loss
rows.operation_detail: Used the default initialization for the cross-entropy fitting transition experiment.

conditions.value: PyTorch default; weights and biases uniform on [−σ, σ], σ² = 1/fin

rows.measure: Transition N* versus P and depth
rows.baseline: orthogonal initialization used for hinge-loss experiment
rows.value: Transition does not appear to depend on depth or input dimension; compared qualitatively with orthogonal-initialization hinge-loss results.
rows.note: Initialization is confounded with loss, optimizer, normalization, batch size, and schedule; no matched initialization comparison.
rows.check: This duplicates the cross-entropy transition result in R1 as an initialization comparator. Initialization changes together with loss, optimizer, normalization and schedule; neither training-speed nor trainable-depth differences attributable to initialization are measured.

rows.subject: fully-connected network, random data, cross-entropy loss
rows.operation_detail: Trained the cross-entropy transition experiment with batch normalization enabled.
rows.measure: Fitting transition as learning time increases
rows.value: At small times and large P, errors remain and the transition cannot be found; with longer training the N* versus P relation approaches linear behavior.
rows.note: No normalization-free matched control or direct speed/learning-rate-tolerance measure is reported.
rows.check: This repeats R1's training-time dependence with batch normalization present. Without a normalization-free comparison, it cannot establish V6's acceleration or higher learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Random binary data, fully connected networks with cross-entropy or hinge loss at the reported long training durations
reader_labels.reason: The study reports a transition between nonzero and zero fitting loss as parameter count increases, and says all data are fitted on the overparameterized side (R1, R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Random data at short training times and binary MNIST fitting
reader_labels.reason: Errors persist at small training times for large P; MNIST is reduced to binary labels and ten PCA components, so the evidence does not cover CIFAR or multiclass benchmark error (R1, R6, R8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Initialization recipes used in the random-data transition experiments
reader_labels.reason: Default and orthogonal initialization occur in experiments with different losses and other settings, so the study does not isolate initialization's effect on speed or trainable depth (R9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-entropy random-data runs with batch normalization
reader_labels.reason: The study reports fitting transitions and training-time dependence with normalization present, but no controlled normalized versus unnormalized speed or learning-rate comparison (R10).
